title: Time shift: moving the whole waveform

actions.text:
x_shifted = np.sin(2 * np.pi * f1 * (t - 0.25))  # shift the wave right with t-0.25

plt.figure(figsize=(7, 3))
plt.plot(t, x1, label="x1")
plt.plot(t, x_shifted, label="x1 shifted right by 0.25 s")
plt.title("Time shift")
plt.xlabel("Time (s)")
plt.ylabel("Amplitude")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

clips.caption: Next shift the 1 Hz waveform 0.25 s to the right; only the timing changes, not the <c.aqua>frequency</c.aqua> or the shape.

A <c.aqua>time shift</c.aqua> moves the whole waveform along the <c.aqua>time axis</c.aqua>. Here t becomes t minus 0.25, so the waveform moves 0.25 s to the right. Frequency and shape stay; only when it happens changes.
